title: DFM for CNC milling
description: Manufacturability rules for a 3-axis milled part: drillable holes, millable internal corners, stable walls, enough material around holes and enough thread engagement.

axis.description: Tool axis: x, y or z.

max_hole_depth_ratio.description: Largest hole depth / diameter drilled without deep-hole tooling.

min_internal_radius.description: Smallest internal corner radius (mm) = radius of the smallest end mill you accept.

min_wall.description: Thinnest wall (mm): about 0.8 in metal, 1.5 in plastics.

min_hole_web_ratio.description: Material around a hole as a multiple of its diameter.

min_thread_ratio.description: Thread length / nominal diameter: 1.0 steel, 1.5-2.0 aluminium.

rules.citation: Guideline: machining shop practice, standard twist drills reach about 4-5 x diameter without pecking or deep-hole tooling
rules.note: Deeper holes need peck cycles, longer drills or gun drilling.

rules.citation: Guideline: an end mill leaves its own radius in every internal corner parallel to the tool axis; sharp internal corners cannot be milled
rules.note: Add a fillet of at least the cutter radius (ideally 1.3 x) or a dog-bone relief.

rules.citation: Guideline: machining shop practice, walls thinner than about 0.8 mm (metal) or 1.5 mm (plastic) chatter and deflect
Guideline: keep at least half a hole diameter of material between a hole and the nearest edge or hole so the wall does not break out
Guideline: rule of thumb for metric threads, engagement of 1.0 x d in steel and 1.5-2.0 x d in aluminium (see VDI 2230-1 for a verified calculation)
ISO 2768-1:1989, Table 1 (permissible deviations for linear dimensions); process capability per DUCAD guideline
